.claude/docs/services/escher-driver.md: - The command line, through the real `escher-session` binary (seven_guis, unix only): `host_binary` (the host role on `counter`; a host that cannot serve; nine argv rows that are no command), `host_log` (a host on `crud` at `RUST_LOG=trace` while three calls run: one span line per call, no id, name or typed text, under both builds; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a second test, a recording host reading 0 of the recording needles — the kept check's names and its directory's name — on stderr), `host_timer` (the timer host moved by a hosted `advance`), `cli_commands` (every driver command as a process on the four tasks: fields, refusals by status `1`, usage by `2`, session errors by `3`) and `cli_flow` (two POSIX `sh` flows, `counter.sh` and `flight.sh`); since 2026-10-19-session-recording `recording` (3 tests, unix only, and 1 off-unix: the command line and the `mcp` role keep the same check byte for byte, the state directory gone after `stop`; a recording directory open to its group refused before anything runs; the `mcp` role's listing and `help` the same with and without `--record`; off unix, `--record` refused `Unsupported`); since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface `mcp_server` (the `mcp` role completes the Counter flow by tool calls alone; .claude/rules/security.md: - 2026-10-15: A listener or env read that only a test makes — served by no binary, reached by no caller — is no crossing and not the founder's call, yet it is registered as test-only in arch §Occupied Resources and the security plan's environment values before it lands, as `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML` and `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` are (the operator's answer, 2026-10-15).

.claude/rules/testing.md: - 2026-10-19: Code compiled only off unix is unverified on this linux host until a non-unix build reads it — after adding or moving a `#[cfg(unix)]` gate (a file-wide `#![cfg(unix)]` split into per-item gates included), run `cargo check --tests --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p {crate}` before pushing: a helper left calling a gated item compiles here and breaks only the windows job, and `cfg_attr(…, allow(dead_code))` cannot excuse a call to an item configured out.

.claude/rules/verification-harness.md: - 2026-10-06: A boot smoke bounded by `timeout N` exits 124 when the stand stays up, but the Andromeda gate tool reads any entry exit 124 or 137 as its own bound firing (`timeout`), so `expect = ['exit 124']` never reads green — author the entry so its own exit is 0 on the stay-up case, or drive it by hand and record its exit and atoms under the chunk's `evidence/`.
